classification.difficultyReason: Combine a complemented set with another set using union and intersection.

content.prompt: The two Venn diagrams show $A'$ and $B$.

spec.description: Two supplied diagrams in left-to-right order, headed A′ and B. Source grey shading is represented by restrained house blue shading.
spec.mathematics: The first shades the universal set outside A; the second shades all of B, including A intersection B.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent givens visible in the student edition.

spec.description: Unshaded rectangular universal set containing overlapping circles A and B.
spec.mathematics: Four regions: A only, intersection, B only and neither.
spec.answerVisibility: No answer shading in the student diagram.

answer.worked: $A'$ contains everything outside $A$. The union also includes all of $B$, so shade the $B$-only region, the overlap and the region outside both circles. Leave only $A\cap B'$ unshaded.

spec.description: Light blue shading everywhere except A only.

answer.worked: The intersection contains points that are both outside $A$ and inside $B$. Shade only the part of $B$ outside $A$, leaving the overlap unshaded.
